clue.text: Coarse woman demands food supposing we'll go outside

indicators.note: the pair of letters from 'we' will surround the next piece, as the clue says they go outside it

parts.note: the letters of 'we', with the 'll (will) read as part of the instruction

explanation.surface: A rough woman insists on a meal, on condition that the speakers step outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demands' looks like the verb of the sentence but is only a link; 'go outside' is the container signal, with 'we'll' split as 'we' plus 'will'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishwife was a woman selling fish, and the word came to mean a loud, foul-mouthed woman.

clue.text: Wilder top of fallen flower

indicators.note: top of means only the first letter of the word is taken, as this is a down clue

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A wilder bloom is described as the head of a dropped flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Faster is a comparative meaning wilder, as in living a fast life.

clue.text: Tempestuous, having got married in a novel

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

explanation.surface: A stormy relationship begins with a wedding in a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy and tempestuous are synonyms, both meaning turbulent.

clue.text: Comic's full of spirit, carrying on

indicators.note: full of means the comic contains the spirit

parts.note: a wag is a joker or comic; the 's is part of the link 'is full of'

explanation.surface: A comedian who has been drinking keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' is the container signal; the possessive on 'Comic's' reads as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Waging means carrying on, as in waging a war.

clue.text: Noisy devices, actual one seen in businesses

indicators.note: seen in means the pieces appear inside the firms

explanation.surface: A loud genuine apparatus is spotted at some companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container signal: the genuine article and 'one' sit inside the businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire alarms are devices that make a loud noise to warn of fire.

clue.text: Hot number is extreme

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A temperature reading is said to be off the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The height of something is its extreme point, as in 'the height of folly'.

clue.text: Retired? Semi-true, unfortunately!

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be retired, but this is only partly true.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes someone retired who keeps an honorary title, such as a professor emeritus.

clue.text: Member enters toilet to find clothes

indicators.note: enters means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: the gents is a British term for a men's toilet
an arm is a member, a limb of the body

explanation.surface: A man goes into a lavatory looking for his clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' is the container signal. THE GENTS is the British everyday name for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are articles of clothing, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Dumb animal turns; then I turn

indicators.note: turns means the animal's name is read the other way

explanation.surface: A mute creature turns around, then the speaker does too.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means saying little, which is close to dumb in the sense of speechless.

clue.text: Entertainer's son's in what manner female?

definitions.note: read as 'Entertainer is', the 's being a link

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a performer's son can be said to be female.
explanation.definitionFit: A showgirl is a woman who sings or dances in a stage show, so a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: This system gives me a trick, all but

indicators.note: all but means nearly all, so the final letter of the trick is dropped

parts.note: a synonym is not needed: the word trick itself

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a measuring system plays them false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' removes the last letter of TRICK to leave TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric system is the decimal system of measurement, which the clue calls this system.

clue.text: One of those hard cheeses: keep 'em in mind

parts.note: 'em is a casual form of them, giving its letters

explanation.surface: Advice to keep certain hard cheeses in your thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a hard Swiss cheese with large holes, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Split second, dividing binary digit

indicators.note: the second piece sits in the middle of the first, dividing it in two

parts.note: a bit is a binary digit, a 0 or 1

explanation.surface: A split second is described as dividing a computer digit.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut in two, which is to split.

clue.text: Suffering relatives who try to solve others' problems

definitions.text: who try to solve others' problems
definitions.note: a description of advice columnists, standing for the people themselves

explanation.surface: Kinsfolk in pain try to sort out other people's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony aunts are newspaper advice columnists who answer readers' letters about personal problems.

clue.text: US agent involved with nugget bars

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled up, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American agent is caught up with some bars of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangbuster is a US law officer who breaks up criminal gangs, so a type of agent.

clue.text: Beat, but it's the other way in pursuit

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
the other way means the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Something is beaten, yet the reverse holds in a chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way' turns round the letters of 'it's', and 'in' sets them inside the pursuit; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise can mean to punish physically, to beat.

clue.text: Furore I'd dispersed, leading to coolness

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An uproar dies away, leaving a chilly atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' rearranges FUROREID; 'leading to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Froideur is a French borrowing for coldness or aloofness in manner.

clue.text: What does not burn is best put in an urgent message

indicators.note: put in means the word best goes inside the message

explanation.surface: Advice that a fireproof material is best mentioned in an emergency call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' is the container signal; 'is' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a mineral fibre that resists fire, so it does not burn.

clue.text: Persecution of Mrs Gamp turning to men in the street

indicators.note: turning means the name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Sarah (Sairey) Gamp is the drunken nurse in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A Dickens character is mistreated as she turns to men in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the name and 'in' is the container signal. Mrs Gamp, Dickens's nurse, is called Sarah (she says Sairey), which the solver must know.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassment is persistent unwanted pressure or intimidation, close in meaning to persecution.

clue.text: Girl always found in the bar

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Girl always found in the bar' (BERTHA): THE BAR is an anagram of the answer but no word signals it, and 'always' gives no letters; no sound parse found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Girl always found in the bar

clue.text: Gathering coal is unnatural

indicators.note: unnatural means not in the natural state, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Collecting fuel is said to be against nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a party or gathering, a noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Produced by an artist standing up and keeping time

indicators.note: keeping means holding the next piece inside
standing up means the name is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: A painting by an artist who stands and keeps the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' reverses DEGAS to SAGED, and 'keeping' puts T inside after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that is staged is produced for the theatre.

clue.text: Made dirty when lubricated with sulphur

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Something becomes grubby once greased with a smelly element.
explanation.definitionFit: Soiled is a past form meaning stained or dirtied.

clue.text: A girl might dance like this, but a judge must wear a shoe

definitions.text: A girl might dance like this

indicators.note: the boot is worn by the following pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a boot is a shoe, taking 'a' as part of the phrase
a referee, or ref, is a judge in sport

explanation.surface: A dancer goes unshod, yet a magistrate must keep a shoe on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must wear' is the container signal: the judge, with 'a', goes inside the shoe; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancing barefoot means without shoes, the manner the definition describes.

clue.text: Imagine a fish about to swallow

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular
to swallow food is to eat it; ate is its past form

explanation.surface: Someone pictures a fish about to gulp something down.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form an idea in the mind, which is to imagine.

clue.text: In Germany, thin girls can eat this!

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: In Germany slender young women supposedly eat whatever they like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' hides the answer across Germany, thin and girls; 'this' stands for the answer as what girls can eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying thin girls can eat anything works as the sentence's own meaning, the answer filling in for 'this'.

clue.text: Looking back at special fabric in the doorway

indicators.note: looking back means the fabric's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric

explanation.surface: Someone glances back at a fancy material in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking back at' reverses SERGE to EGRES.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out, and a doorway is one such exit point.

clue.text: Being troubled, a seaman at first left port

indicators.note: at first means just the opening letter of the sailor word is used

parts.note: a ship that left port sailed

explanation.surface: A distressed sailor set out from harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Assailed means attacked or beset, so being troubled by something.
